summary: A correction to BBN Report 1822: a page was wrong about when a host is marked dead. In fact the timeout has always been 30 seconds and the host was never marked dead under the stated conditions. This is an error in the report, not a change to the IMP system.

plainLanguage.summary: This note corrects a description in BBN Report 1822. The timeout was 30 seconds, and it did not mark the host dead under the conditions discussed.

questions: how does imp detect dead hosts
subtitle: A correction to a timeout statement in BBN Report 1822 about the IMP system.

tldr.problem: BBN found errors in Report 1822's description of when a host is marked dead and how long a timeout lasts.
tldr.mechanism: The corrected page states that the timeout is 30 seconds and that the host is not marked dead under the stated conditions; two lines on the next page should be deleted.
tldr.outcome: The RFC stresses that these are errors in the report, not changes to the IMP system, which already behaved this way.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 270 as Unknown, with no RFC recorded as updating or obsoleting it. It corrects documentation about the IMP system.

sections.title: The Report Error
sections.content:
While preparing RFC 271, Alex McKenzie found errors in BBN Report 1822. RFC 270 supplies a corrected version of page 25 and says to remove the first two lines of page 26.

The correction changes the account of the host's status and the length of the timeout described in the report.
sections.plainLanguage: A review of another report found that its description did not match the IMP system. This RFC identifies the page that needs correction.

sections.title: The Corrected Timeout
sections.content:
The corrected text says the host is not marked dead under the stated conditions. It also gives the timeout period as 30 seconds rather than 40 seconds.

RFC 270 notes that the timeout was always 30 seconds and that the host was never marked dead in this case.
sections.plainLanguage: The report had the wrong timeout and host-status description. The actual behavior was already the corrected version.

sections.title: A Documentation Correction
sections.content: McKenzie emphasizes that the changes correct earlier versions of Report 1822 and do not change the IMP system. The RFC says a more formal update to the report would be distributed later.
sections.plainLanguage: No system change is proposed here. The note fixes the written explanation and says a fuller report revision was planned.
